I was compelled to include an introductory chapter to this revised version of ""Soul-Trapping"" after the ethical arguments that sprang from the publication of the first edition.
Soul-trapping is the art of taking a creature's soul upon death and confining it in an appropriately-sized phylactery.
Some mages would argue that, once dead and soul-trapped, a creature's spirit is merely an echo of its previous life, no longer aware of what goes on around it.
Even those rare individuals who become phantasmal hunters lurking the darkness of Tamriel are nothing more than predators acting on natural impulses.
As such, they argue, soul-trapping is not unethical.
